name: GM - Bowling Green Assembly, Bowling Green KY

fieldNotes.facility: GM Bowling Green Assembly Plant, 600 Corvette Dr, Bowling Green KY 42101 - the sole U.S. plant building the Chevrolet Corvette (since 1981, ~1.7M sq ft). Positively confirmed: Street View off the south frontage shows the building face carrying a large 'PROUDLY ASSEMBLED IN BOWLING GREEN' Corvette mural; the site sits immediately off I-65 Exit 28 directly across from the National Corvette Museum, with the NCM Motorsports Park track to the SE - all consistent with the published location. Geocode for the street address lands near the south employee/visitor entrance; the true building centroid is ~37.0103,-86.3658.
fieldNotes.truckGate: Secured single-building GM assembly campus. Perimeter is fenced/landscaped-buffered with controlled access; the truck/materials approach runs in from the SW off the Corvette Dr / I-65 frontage and feeds enclosed truck wells on the NW building face. Public Street View panos sit on the south frontage and employee-lot loops and do not reach the interior truck gate itself, so the gate structure is inferred from layout plus standard GM plant security practice rather than directly imaged - marked uncertain.
fieldNotes.guardShack: GM assembly plants run staffed security gatehouses at controlled truck entrances. A small control-booth footprint is consistent with the SW materials approach, but it could not be crisply isolated in overhead imagery (tree cover and the secured interior); Street View cannot reach it. Held at guardShack:true with remoteGs:false on plant-class precedent but flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: Materials docks are largely enclosed truck wells integrated into the NW/W building face rather than an open banked dock wall; ~20-25 door positions estimated from roof penetrations, dock canopies and the trailers staged against the NW face. Band 10-25, marked uncertain - overhead-only estimate.
fieldNotes.dropYard: A modest trailer drop/marshalling area sits against the NW building face (just-in-time/just-in-sequence parts staging) with ~14 trailers visible and room for ~40. This is active sequencing staging, not a large standalone trailer storage lot - hence dropArea 10-25, dropYard true, scale false.
fieldNotes.shipRcvSeparate: Inbound parts/materials are received on the NW/W truck-well side; finished Corvettes dispatch from the opposite (E/SE) side adjacent to the large finished-vehicle storage lots - shipping and receiving run from physically separate clusters.
fieldNotes.railServed: The CSX mainline runs along the NW/N edge of the property; a siding/spur curves toward the plant's NW corner. Inbound rail materials staging is consistent with the rail buffer inside the north fence line. railServed:true.
fieldNotes.fastLaneOpportunity: Wide paved aprons and a long internal approach drive from the frontage to the docks leave unused width for an express/bypass lane - fastLaneOpportunity true.
fieldNotes.drivewayLong: Long internal gate-to-dock approach (several hundred feet from the frontage to the NW truck wells) can hold a 3+ truck queue - drivewayLong true.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Edge-of-town interstate-exit setting on the north side of Bowling Green (a small Kentucky city), surrounded by I-65, open fields, the Corvette Museum and a motorsports park rather than dense metro fabric - classed Rural per rubric.
fieldNotes.buildingCount: Treated as 2: the main integrated assembly building plus the NW production wing/annex reaching toward the rail. Ancillary structures (wastewater plant, lobby) not counted as primary buildings.
fieldNotes.siteAreaAcres: ~235 acres derived from the traced perimeter polygon (building + employee parking + finished-vehicle lots + rail buffer inside the fence).
fieldNotes.scale: No truck scale/weigh platform clearly identified in the truck path - scale false.
fieldNotes.multiStep: No clearly imaged second checkpoint after the gate; left false.

citations.claim: GM media facility page lists Bowling Green Assembly, Bowling Green KY as the GM-operated plant building the Chevrolet Corvette
GM newsroom: Corvette ZR1s being built at Bowling Green Assembly; sole Corvette plant, actively producing

verification.rationale: GM-operated sole U.S. Corvette plant, actively producing in 2026 (2026 MY concluded May 2026, 2027 MY starting; spring supplier pauses were temporary). Kept by New GM in 2009 (not divested to Motors Liquidation/RACER).
